newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Intertie up to 6,250 MW as of late Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Intertie up to 6,250 MW as of late Thurs.

text.p: Capacity on the Pacific Intertie high-voltage power transmission lines, linking the Northwest to Southern California, was increased to 6,250 megawatts (MW) late Thursday, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Monday.
The lines, which have a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, had been capped at 5,200 MW since late last summer when two widespread power blackouts hit the West.
The capacity is now split at 3,568 MW for the AC (alternating current) portion of the intertie, and 2,682 MW for the DC (direct current) portion, BPA said.
Due to maintenance scheduled for Tuesday morning, the DC capacity will be cut slightly, while the AC's will be increased by the same amount.
The Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) is currently reviewing plans to raise the interite capacity to between 7,000 MW and 7,800 MW, with a final decision expected in late April.
